tldr: A run of arXiv papers on how agents learn from their own trajectories. ClueFlow credits search steps by research-state transitions, a memory-skill paper tackles lifelong learning under a bounded context window, and a video-editing RL paper asks when fine-grained credit assignment fails to help.
whats_new: CausalXRL adds an interpretability angle, using causal graph reasoning to explain reinforcement-learning agents' behavior.
why_it_matters: Credit assignment, memory design, and explainability determine how agents improve from experience and whether you can audit why they act as they do.

beats.headline: ClueFlow credits long-horizon search by research-state transitions
Bidirectional memory-skill learning for lifelong agents
Fine-grained credit assignment helps and hurts in multimodal agentic RL
CausalXRL explains RL agents through causal graph reasoning

open_questions: Do ClueFlow-style state-transition rewards hold up beyond the search benchmarks in the paper?
Which task properties predict that fine-grained credit assignment will hurt rather than help?
Do causal-graph explanations from CausalXRL carry over to LLM agents, or only classic RL environments?
take_for_builders: Before adding per-step rewards to an agent RL setup, run an ablation against outcome-only rewards on your own tasks.
